conventions.convention: For n≥2 and 1≤p<n, p*=np/(n-p), so 1/p*=1/p−1/n. No finite Sobolev conjugate is assigned to p≥n.

W₀^{k,p} is the Sobolev-norm closure of compactly supported smooth functions; it does not mean pointwise boundary vanishing. Extension domains are indexed by the fixed pair (k,p); a common operator for all indices is not assumed.
The John condition here is dist(γ(t),∂Ω)≥c⁻¹|x−γ(t)|, with γ starting at x and ending at the distinguished point. Estimates use an admissible constant, not attainment of its infimum.

|Du| is the Euclidean norm of the coordinate weak derivatives. For complex scalars this is the Frobenius norm of the associated real-linear map, not its operator norm; the converse Lipschitz bound is √2L.

The critical first-order finite-q embedding assumes extension operators for every source exponent in (n/2,n), allowed to vary with the exponent. The higher-order theorem instead uses a fixed W^{k,p} extension and a compactly supported whole-space cutoff.

In the higher-order embedding, C^{m,α}(closure Ω) uses derivatives of an ambient representative near closure Ω. Fractional endpoint Hölder regularity is included when k−n/p is nonintegral; integer endpoints are excluded.
Normalized dilations are φ_t(x)=t⁻ⁿφ(x/t). Nontangential maximal functions use the closed cone |y−x|≤at with a≥1; their values may be infinite.
P_N controls weight (1+|x|)^N and derivatives through N+1. The grand maximal function uses aperture one and all tests with P_N≤1, including zero-integral tests.

Atoms are chosen measurable representatives supported in closed nondegenerate axis-parallel cubes, with size ≤|Q|⁻¹/p and moments through s≥floor(n(1/p−1)). Support can change under null-set modifications; size and moments do not. Zero atoms are allowed.
Real Hardy H^p consists of tempered distributions whose fixed admissible radial maximal function belongs to L^p. Its H^1 notation is distinct from the Sobolev H^1=W^{1,2} notation on the PDE pages.

Compact embedding means continuous inclusion with compact closures of bounded images. Its sequential equivalence assumes Countable and Dependent Choice. The Fréchet–Kolmogorov statement supplies sufficiency, and assigns zero to empty-family nonnegative suprema.
Local L^p compactness includes p=1, but Sobolev membership of the extracted limit is asserted only for p>1. Compact Hölder targets use β strictly below the continuous embedding exponent.
The Slobodeckij double integral uses completed product measure and assigns zero on the diagonal. Trace compactness below dimension uses θ=1−1/p, boundary dimension n−1, and target q<(n−1)p/(n−p).

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For n≥1, 0<p<∞ and an admissible Schwartz kernel φ, there is a finite N₀(n,p,φ), independent of f, such that for every N≥N₀ and f∈S′, radial L^p membership, nontangential L^p membership for some/every aperture a≥1, and grand-maximal L^p membership are equivalent, with the stated two-sided bounds and kernel independence.

Assume Countable Choice. For 0<p≤1, f∈H^p, s=floor(n(1/p−1)), a reproducing pair of integer flatness K≥n/p, and the stated admissible N, there is a countable atomic representation f=Σλ_Ba_B in S′ with positive coefficients and Σλ_B^p≤C‖f‖_{H^p}^p. Its atoms have the stated 7B support, size and moments.

Assume Countable Choice and the stated kernel, reproducing order and admissible grand-maximal order. For n≥1 and 0<p≤1, f∈H^p iff f admits an ℓ^p sum of (p,∞,floor(n(1/p−1)))-atoms converging in S′. The H^p quasi-norm is equivalent to the infimum of the coefficient ℓ^p quasi-norms; every such series also converges in H^p.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let n≥2, 1<p<n and p*=np/(n−p). There is C(n,p) such that ‖u‖_{L^{p*}(Rⁿ)}≤C(n,p)‖Du‖_{L^p(Rⁿ)} for every u∈W^{1,p}(Rⁿ;K), with Euclidean weak-gradient magnitude.

Assume AC, n≥2, a bounded W^{k,p}-extension domain, k≥1, 1≤p<∞ and u∈W^{k,p}. If kp<n, the stated bound holds for 1≤q≤np/(n−kp); if kp=n, for every finite q; if kp>n, for C^{m,α}(closure Ω) whenever 0<α<1 and m+α<k−n/p, also at the specified nonintegral fractional endpoint.

Assume Countable and Dependent Choice. For 1≤p<∞, an L^p(Rⁿ) family satisfying uniform norm boundedness, uniformly small tails and uniform translation continuity is totally bounded, has compact closure, and every sequence in it has an L^p-convergent subsequence. Empty-family suprema are zero.
Assume AC. For n≥1, a bounded W^{1,p}-extension domain Ω and 1≤p<∞, W^{1,p}(Ω) is compactly embedded in L^p(Ω); every bounded C¹ domain is an example.
Assume AC. For n≥1, bounded open Ω and 1≤p<∞, W₀^{1,p}(Ω) is compactly embedded in L^p(Ω), with no boundary regularity required.
Assume Countable Choice. If Ω is open and lies in a slab a<x·e<b for a unit vector e and a<b, then for 1≤p<∞ every u∈W₀^{1,p}(Ω;K) satisfies ‖u‖_p≤C(p)(b−a)‖Du‖_p. The proof obtains C(p)=1.
Assume AC. On a nonempty bounded connected extension domain Ω⊂Rⁿ, n≥1, for 1≤p<∞ there is C(Ω,p) such that ‖u−u_Ω‖_p≤C‖Du‖_p for every u∈W^{1,p}(Ω;K).
Assume Countable Choice. For n≥2, 1≤p<∞, a ball B and u∈W^{1,p}(B;K), |u(z)−u_B|≤C(n)∫_B|Du(y)||z−y|^{1−n}dy for almost every z∈B.

Assume AC. For n≥2, n<p<∞, open Ω and u∈W^{1,p}(Ω;K), there is a continuous representative u*. On every B(x,r) with B(x,2r) compactly contained in Ω, |u*(z)−u*(y)|≤C(n,p)|z−y|^{1−n/p}‖Du‖_{L^p(B(x,2r))} for z,y∈B(x,r).
Assume Countable Choice. For d≥1, 0<θ<1, 1≤p<∞ and pθ<d, with p⋆=dp/(d−pθ), every measurable compactly supported real f satisfies ‖f‖_{p⋆}^p≤C(d,p,θ)[f]_{θ,p}^p, interpreted with extended values.
Assume AC. For d≥1, 0<θ<1, 1≤p<∞ and pθ<d, a family bounded in W^{θ,p}(Rᵈ) and supported in one fixed bounded set is relatively compact in L^q(Rᵈ) for every 1≤q<dp/(d−pθ).

concerns.concern: The Remark says: “Bounded C¹ and bounded Lipschitz domains satisfy the uniform interior cone condition, and every nonempty bounded connected open set satisfying that uniform condition is a John domain ...; hence the inequality applies to those classes as well.” The final inference appears to omit connectedness for the C¹/Lipschitz classes. The opened published definition def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal explicitly says “Connectedness is not required.” Two disjoint balls therefore qualify as a bounded smooth domain, while the owned cex-poincare-wirtinger-needs-connectedness proves that a single-global-mean Poincaré inequality fails there. Resolve the scope of “those classes” by retaining the connectedness qualification.

alerts.finding: Proof 5.1 says that “the uniform energy dissipation ε_j∫₀ᵀ∫|∇u^j|²≤½‖u₀‖₂² supplies only a uniform gradient bound”. As ε_j→0, this displayed estimate supplies a uniform bound for √ε_j∇u^j, while the unweighted gradient bound it yields grows like ε_j⁻¹/². The wording should identify the bound as weighted. The seam's actual Fréchet–Kolmogorov invocation in F6/Proof 3.1 uses separately established translation moduli.

seams_checked.note: Opened the page and the seven direct citing items. Atom pairings retain cube support, size and zeroth-moment cancellation. The L2-atom lemma states the actual grand test seminorm and admissible order, and uses maximal characterization after proving grand-maximal integrability. Finite-sum density and bounded BMO pairings use the p=1 atomic representation and H¹ tail convergence under Countable Choice; the general BMO functional theorem assumes AC.

Opened the page and both citing remarks. They identify H¹ through the owned radial-maximal definition. The square-function equivalence is explicitly recorded externally, restricted to L¹ inputs and homogeneous scales j∈Z; neither remark attributes it to the owned maximal theorem or extends the distinct inhomogeneous theorem to an endpoint.

Opened the page and lem-vanishing-viscosity-families-are-locally-precompact-in-lone. F6 states the L¹ Fréchet–Kolmogorov conclusion with boundedness, tails and uniform translation continuity, retaining CC/DC. Proof 3.1 applies it in dimension n+1 to compactly supported spacetime cutoffs after verifying both spatial and temporal translation control. The separate energy-bound wording alert does not change this citation.

Opened the page and its five direct citing items. The Neumann theorem/F3 uses connected-domain Poincaré–Wirtinger at p=2 on a nonempty bounded W^{1,2}-extension domain. F8/Proof 1.3 states and uses bounded H¹-to-L² Rellich extraction; the disconnected extension is proved separately. The four Dirichlet consumers also faithfully specialize the group's slab Poincaré inequality to p=2. Their AC/CC premises suffice for the current supplier's CC hypothesis.
